title: Quantitatively Measuring In situ Flows using a Self-Contained Underwater Velocimetry Apparatus (SCUVA)
protocol: Ensure all SCUVA components have sufficient battery power and recording tape.
Select video camera resolution and frame rates for best DPIV results.
Clean o-ring grooves and o-rings with a clean towel or wipe.
Spread manufacturer-provided o-ring grease evenly on the o-rings.
Replace the greased o-rings in the housing grooves.
Clean the laser and camera housing apertures to prevent deformation.
Submerge both empty housings in a tub of water for 5 to 10 minutes.
Remove the housings from the water and towel dry the outside.
Check for moisture inside the housings after drying.
Use disposable, paper moisture strips during the pressure test.
Place SCUVA components inside the housings after passing the pressure test.
Attach high-intensity discharge (HID) light pods to the camera housing.
Orient the lights so they illuminate the area directly ahead without interfering with grip on handles and operation of controls.
Ensure proper alignment of the laser beam relative to the optical lens in low-light conditions.
Align the laser/lens combination to create a vertical sheet of light perpendicular to the camera housing.
Use temperature-sensitive paper to determine the orientation of the laser sheet.
Connect the laser housing to the camera housing using SCUVA attachments and the rigid, extendable arm.
Firmly attach both housings to prevent rotation with respect to each other.
Conduct measurement dives only in low-light locations or at nighttime to avoid natural light interference.
Wait until dusk or later before entering the water for measurements.
Turn on the camera housing before entering the water.
Immerse SCUVA in water and attach the apparatus to yourself using a line.
Release SCUVA once attached to determine buoyancy characteristics.
Attach buoyancy foam or lead weights as needed for neutral buoyancy.
Switch on the laser and hold the apparatus stationary.
Position the laser using the extendable arm far from the diver.
Adjust the camera zoom until the field of view frames the target and surrounding fluid.
Focus the video camera on the laser sheet until particles appear sharp and in focus.
Switch the camera to manual focus mode.
Calibrate SCUVA by placing an object with known dimensions in the laser sheet within the video camera's field of view.
Record for several seconds during calibration.
Extract an image from the recorded video sequence after the dive.
Determine a calibration constant that converts the field of view size from pixels to cm.
Reposition the extendable arm or change the camera zoom if the operator adjusts the field of view size during the dive.
Begin the dive by descending to the working depth.
Upon finding a target, determine the environmental bulk flow properties.
Observe bubbles exhaled from the diver to infer the direction of current surrounding the target.
Release a small quantity of fluorescent dye (fluorescein) if needed to determine the current direction.
Position the diver and SCUVA relative to the target based on the direction of current or bulk flow, ensuring the diver is not located upstream of the target.
Position the laser sheet parallel to the direction of current to maximize particle residence time within the laser sheet.
If no current or bulk flow is present, position the diver and SCUVA relative to the target unrestricted.
Position SCUVA to illuminate and record fluid motion surrounding a target.
Predict the location of a moving target and position SCUVA accordingly while remaining motionless.
Begin recording as the target moves through the camera’s field of view.
Frame the target and surrounding fluid in the video camera’s field of view for a stationary target.
Begin recording while remaining motionless when the target is stationary.
Refrain from rotational and out-of-plane motions during video recording.
Turn off all components of SCUVA upon completion of video collection.
Restore the laser arm to its retracted position.
Remove SCUVA from the water after video collection.
Detach the camera and laser housings from the arm.
Rinse or soak the apparatus in fresh water before drying.
Dry the housings thoroughly.
Remove components from the housings.
Recharge and replace batteries if needed for another dive.
Connect the video camera to a computer.
Extract video from the HD tape using HD video software (e.g., Adobe Premiere Pro or iMovie).
Determine the range of video for conversion into images for DPIV analysis.
Import the extracted images into a DPIV processing program (e.g., DaVis or MatPIV).
Select calibration constant and image capture parameters as prompted by the DPIV software.
Generate velocity fields from consecutive particle images using the DPIV software.
Apply additional post-processing steps depending on measurement quality and type.
